text: Semiconductor stocks under one hundred rupees. Everyone is hunting the next multibagger. But look closer, because some of these are traps.
Meet SPEL Semiconductor, from Chennai. It packs and tests computer chips, and calls itself India's first company to do it. Sounds perfect, right?
Here's the catch. Its factory has been shut since January fourteenth. Last year, sales were just six crore rupees, and the loss was twenty four crore.
Yet the market still values it at about three hundred fifty eight crore. And the share has already fallen fifty one percent from its high.
Next, M I C Electronics, at thirty five rupees. Its main business is LED displays. Analysts warn that many tiny stocks claim a chip link that is weak.
Then Artificial Electronics, at thirty seven rupees. Down seventy nine percent, and under exchange surveillance. That is a red flag.
So where is the real chip business? Just above one hundred rupees. R I R Power Electronics is building India's first silicon carbide chip plant, in Odisha. A six hundred eighteen crore project.
And MosChip designs chips. Both are real chip businesses. But both are still down more than thirty percent from their highs.
Before you buy any chip penny stock, check three things. Is the factory running? Is it making a profit? Is it on the surveillance list?
A low price does not mean cheap. Save this, and follow money in cloud. Not a buy or sell call.
